analysis.subject: maths
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers right triangle definitions, sine cosine and tangent ratios as functions of angle, ladder illustration showing ratio depends only on angle with Pythagorean check, and complementary relation and table use for solving triangle problems.

overview.headline: Right triangle ratios define sine cosine tangent as functions of angle

keyPoints.point: A right triangle contains one angle equal to 90 degrees and triangle properties show angle sum relation
keyPoints.quote: A right triangle is a three sided figure with one angle equal to 90 degrees.

keyPoints.point: Sine is ratio of opposite side to hypotenuse for right triangle
keyPoints.quote: We will call the ratio of the opposite side of a right triangle to the hypotenuse the sine and give it the symbol sin.

keyPoints.point: Ladder example shows ratio stays same for any right triangle with same angle
keyPoints.quote: The ratio stays the same for any right triangle with a 75.5 degree angle.

keyPoints.point: Ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse is function of angle and varies with angle change
keyPoints.quote: The ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse is a function of the angle c, so we can write the symbol as cos(c) = value.

keyTerms.gloss: longest side opposite right angle across triangle
keyTerms.quote: We define the side of the triangle opposite from the right angle to be the hypotenuse.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of opposite side to hypotenuse depending on angle
keyTerms.quote: We will call the ratio of the opposite side of a right triangle to the hypotenuse the sine and give it the symbol sin.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse varying with angle
keyTerms.quote: The ratio of the adjacent side of a right triangle to the hypotenuse is called the cosine and given the symbol cos.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of opposite side to adjacent side for angle
keyTerms.quote: Finally, the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side is called the tangent and given the symbol tan.

keyTerms.gloss: relationship where ratio value depends uniquely on angle
keyTerms.quote: The ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse is a function of the angle c, so we can write the symbol as cos(c) = value.
